newsitem.title: USA: Parker Hannifin adopts holder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Parker Hannifin adopts holder rights plan.

text.p: Parker Hannifin Corp on Monday said its board adopted a shareholder rights plan that would replace one expiring on February 17.
Duane Collins, president and chief executive officer, said the plan was adopted as a preventive measure and not in response to any specific effort to acquire the company.
He said it was intended to deter abusive takeover tactics that can be used to deprive shareholders of the full value of their investments.

Collins said the rights plan would not have a dilutive effect on earnings and would not affect reported earnings per share. He said the plan was not taxable to the company or to its shareholders, and would not change the way in which the company's shares are traded.
The plan, which is typically called called a "poison pill" anti-takeover measure, would be triggered when a group or a person acquires 15 percent or more of the company's common stock.
The company said it has declared a dividend of one right for each common share held. The dividend is payable on February 18 to stockholders of record as of February 17.

Each right, other than those held by the potential acquirer, will entitle the holder to buy common shares having a market value of twice the exercise price of the right. The right is exercisable 10 days after announcement by a person or a group of the acquistion of 15 percent or more of the company's common stock, it said.
